  measurement pipeline from Oct 12, 2026 (higher counts, slightly lower play-through rate) — don't read the
  jump as a real change.
- **Before launch**: invite up to 10 friends or group members as early testers from the publish flow.
- **Player Support** (early access, age-checked 13+): add an in-game "report a problem" button that calls
  `SocialService:PromptFeedbackSubmissionAsync({ FeedbackType = Enum.FeedbackType.PlayerSupport })`
  (client, `pcall`); reports arrive with device info and screenshots in Creator Hub → Audience → Player Support.

## Related skills

`roblox-monetization` (offers, pricing), `roblox-data-stores` (streaks, season data),
`roblox-open-cloud` (configs/experiments/notifications APIs), `roblox-game-systems`.

skills.name: gh-el-roblox-game-systems
skills.description: Recipes for common systems built on server authority - currency service and leaderstats, XP/levels, round loops with intermission and teams, validated melee/ranged combat, inventory and tools, soft-currency shops, obby checkpoints, daily rewards, pets. Use when implementing or reviewing gameplay systems such as rounds, combat, weapons, inventories, shops, currencies, or progression.
skills.body:
# Game systems recipes

Every recipe follows the same contract:
1. **State lives on the server** in a service module; persistent parts go through the data layer
   (`roblox-data-stores`).
2. **Clients send intents** through validated, rate-limited remotes (`roblox-security`,
   `roblox-networking`) and render state they receive (attributes, snapshots/deltas).
3. **Config is data**: tunables in a shared/server config module (or live `ConfigService` configs).
4. **Lifecycle-safe**: handles late joiners, respawns, leaving mid-action, and server shutdown.

| System | Reference |
| --- | --- |
| Leaderstats, currency service, XP/levels, daily rewards, obby checkpoints | [references/progression.md](references/progression.md) |
| Round loop (intermission → match → results), teams, spawning | [references/round-system.md](references/round-system.md) |
| Melee and ranged combat with server validation, cooldowns, damage attribution | [references/combat.md](references/combat.md) |
| Inventory, equipping tools, shop purchases (soft currency), pets that follow | [references/inventory-shop.md](references/inventory-shop.md) |

## Currency service (the pattern every economy uses)

```luau
--!strict
-- ServerScriptService/Server/Services/CurrencyService.luau
local Players = game:GetService("Players")

type Balances = { [Player]: number }

local MAX_BALANCE = 1e12

local CurrencyService = {}
local balances: Balances = {}

local function publish(player: Player)
	player:SetAttribute("Coins", balances[player]) -- replicated to every client; UI listens
end

function CurrencyService.load(player: Player, saved: number?)
	balances[player] = math.clamp(saved or 0, 0, MAX_BALANCE)
	publish(player)
end

function CurrencyService.get(player: Player): number
	return balances[player] or 0
end

-- Positive amount only; returns the new balance.
function CurrencyService.add(player: Player, amount: number, _source: string): number?
	local balance = balances[player]
	if balance == nil or not math.isfinite(amount) or amount <= 0 then
		return nil
	end
	balances[player] = math.min(balance + math.floor(amount), MAX_BALANCE)
	publish(player)
	return balances[player]
end

-- Atomic check-and-spend; false if insufficient.
function CurrencyService.spend(player: Player, amount: number, _sink: string): boolean
	local balance = balances[player]
	if balance == nil or not math.isfinite(amount) or amount <= 0 or balance < amount then
		return false
	end
	balances[player] = balance - math.floor(amount)
	publish(player)
	return true
end

Players.PlayerRemoving:Connect(function(player)
	balances[player] = nil -- after the data layer has saved it
end)

return CurrencyService
```

- One module owns each resource; nothing else writes it. Log sources/sinks to analytics
  (`roblox-analytics-liveops`).
- The in-memory balance is saved by the data layer (ProfileStore `profile.Data.coins`) — or make the
  profile table the balance store directly.
- For display, clients read `player:GetAttribute("Coins")` and `GetAttributeChangedSignal("Coins")`.
  `leaderstats` (a Folder with `IntValue`s under the player) shows values in the player list.

## Design checklist for any new system

- [ ] Where does authoritative state live, and how is it persisted?
- [ ] What can the client request, and how is each request validated and rate-limited?
- [ ] What happens on join mid-session, respawn, leave, teleport, and server shutdown?
- [ ] How is it tuned (config) and measured (analytics)?
- [ ] How does it behave with 1 player, full servers, and high latency?
- [ ] Is it streaming-safe on the client?

## Related skills

`roblox-architecture`, `roblox-security`, `roblox-data-stores`, `roblox-networking`,
`roblox-characters-animation`, `roblox-monetization`, `roblox-ui`.

skills.name: gh-el-roblox-text-chat
skills.description: Chat and text safety - TextChatService (channels, SendAsync, ShouldDeliverCallback, OnIncomingMessage, commands, bubbles, custom UI, platform-integrated chat and TextChannelWindow migration due May 2027), mandatory TextService filtering of any player-authored text, rate limits, privacy checks, PolicyService restrictions, legacy Chat migration. Use when adding chat features or commands, or any feature that shows one player's text to others (names, signs, notes).
skills.body:
# Chat and text safety

## Non-negotiable rules (Roblox Community Standards)

1. Player-to-player conversation must go through **TextChatService** `TextChannel`s (handles filtering,
   privacy/parental settings, and abuse reporting). The legacy `Chat` service/`ChatService` Lua modules
   are gone — `TextChatService` is the only chat system.
2. **Any text authored by one player and shown to another** (pet names, signs, guild names, trade notes,
   custom UI) must be filtered with `TextService:FilterStringAsync` on the server before display — and
   re-filtered when loaded from a DataStore later.
3. Editable text others can see (signs, bulletin boards) needs a rate limit of at least 1 minute.
4. Respect privacy settings with `CanUserChatAsync`/`CanUsersChatAsync`/`CanUsersDirectChatAsync` and mark
   direct-message channels with `TextChannel:SetDirectChatRequester()`.

Not chat (no filtering needed): your own UI text, game status messages, admin announcements you write.

## Filtering player-authored text

```luau
--!strict
local TextService = game:GetService("TextService")

-- Broadcast (e.g. a sign everyone sees). Returns nil if filtering failed: then show nothing.
local function filterForEveryone(text: string, fromUserId: number): string?
	local ok, result = pcall(function()
		local filterResult = TextService:FilterStringAsync(text, fromUserId, Enum.TextFilterContext.PublicChat)
		return filterResult:GetNonChatStringForBroadcastAsync()
	end)
	return if ok then result else nil
end

-- Per-recipient (respects each viewer's age/settings; e.g. a private note).
local function filterForUser(text: string, fromUserId: number, toUserId: number): string?
	local ok, result = pcall(function()
		local filterResult = TextService:FilterStringAsync(text, fromUserId, Enum.TextFilterContext.PrivateChat)
		return filterResult:GetNonChatStringForUserAsync(toUserId)
	end)
	return if ok then result else nil
end

return { forEveryone = filterForEveryone, forUser = filterForUser }
```

- Filter on the **server**, after the player submits (not per keystroke); rate-limit and length-cap first.
- On failure, **fail closed** (show nothing / a placeholder), never the raw text.
- Store the raw text if you must, but always filter at display time (filters and viewer settings change).
- Numbers-only or short strings can still be filtered (hashtags `###`); design UI for that.

## TextChatService essentials

- Defaults: `CreateDefaultTextChannels` creates `RBXGeneral` and `RBXSystem`; `CreateDefaultCommands`
  adds built-ins (`/whisper`, `/team`, `/mute`, ...). Configure look via `ChatWindowConfiguration`,
  `ChatInputBarConfiguration`, `BubbleChatConfiguration` (or disable and build your own UI with
  `TextChannel:SendAsync` and `TextChatService.MessageReceived`).
- Flow: client `TextChannel:SendAsync(text)` → server `TextChannel.ShouldDeliverCallback(message, textSource)`
  per recipient → filtering → clients' `OnIncomingMessage` callbacks → display.
- Callbacks must **not yield**. `ShouldDeliverCallback` is server-only; `TextChatService.OnIncomingMessage`
  and `TextChannel.OnIncomingMessage` are client-only (formatting).
- System messages: `channel:DisplaySystemMessage(text)` on the client (local only).
- Custom channels (team, party, proximity): create `TextChannel`s under `TextChatService` on the server,
  `channel:AddUserAsync(userId)` to add members; check the returned `TextSource`'s `CanSend`.

```luau
--!strict
-- Client: chat tags and colors via OnIncomingMessage (formatting only; never yields).
local Players = game:GetService("Players")
local TextChatService = game:GetService("TextChatService")

TextChatService.OnIncomingMessage = function(message: TextChatMessage)
	local properties = Instance.new("TextChatMessageProperties")
	local source = message.TextSource
	if source then
		local player = Players:GetPlayerByUserId(source.UserId)
		if player and player:GetAttribute("VIP") then
			properties.PrefixText = `<font color="#F5CD30">[VIP]</font> {message.PrefixText}`
		end
	end
	return properties
end
```

```luau
--!strict
-- Server: a /spawn command, restricted to admins.
local Players = game:GetService("Players")
local TextChatService = game:GetService("TextChatService")

local ADMINS: { [number]: boolean } = { [123456] = true }

local command = Instance.new("TextChatCommand")
command.Name = "SpawnCommand"
command.PrimaryAlias = "/spawn"
command.Parent = TextChatService

command.Triggered:Connect(function(source: TextSource, unfilteredText: string)
	if not ADMINS[source.UserId] then
		return
	end
	local player = Players:GetPlayerByUserId(source.UserId)
	print(`{player and player.Name} ran: {unfilteredText}`)
end)
```

## Platform-integrated chat (required May 2027)

Roblox is making chat native. Opt in to test now: select `TextChatService` in Studio and set
`PlatformIntegratedChat = Enabled` (Studio only, not scriptable). When enabled:
- Roblox renders all chat, in the default window or `TextChannelWindow`s you place in UI (one per
  `TextChannel` via `Target`; works in `SurfaceGui`s). Custom chat UIs can no longer render messages.
- Message text is hidden from code: `TextChatMessage.Text`/`Translation`/`PrefixText`, `OnIncomingMessage`,
  `Player.Chatted`, and `TextChannel:SendAsync` stop working (return `""` + warning). No chat logging.
- Commands must be `TextChatCommand`s; preset phrases → Quick Words; chat tags/prefixes → role badges
  (planned Feb 2027 — don't opt in yet if you rely on prefixes). `DisplaySystemMessage` and
  `BubbleChatConfiguration`/`OnBubbleAdded` styling still work.
- **New code**: build on `TextChatCommand`, `TextChannelWindow`, and system messages; avoid reading message
  text. The `OnIncomingMessage` tag example above only works until migration.

More: proximity chat, team channels, custom UI, and migrating from legacy chat:
[references/chat-recipes.md](references/chat-recipes.md).

**Quick Words** (preset safe phrases for all ages, for coordinating where free chat is limited): add game-specific
ones in Creator Hub → game → Configure → Chat → Quick Words — up to 3 categories of 3–10 phrases, in English
(auto-translated), reviewed before going live. They replace the default categories; General stays.

## PolicyService (per-user restrictions)

`PolicyService:GetPolicyInfoForPlayerAsync(player)` (server, `pcall`) returns flags such as
`ArePaidRandomItemsRestricted`, `IsPaidItemTradingAllowed`, `AreAdsAllowed`, `AllowedExternalLinkReferences`,
`IsSubjectToChinaPolicies`, `IsContentSharingAllowed`. Gate loot boxes, trading, ads, and links to
social media (only show platforms listed in `AllowedExternalLinkReferences`) per player.

## Related skills

`roblox-security` (rate limits, validation), `roblox-ui` (text input UI), `roblox-monetization`
(paid random items), `roblox-data-stores` (storing user text).

skills.name: gh-el-roblox-world-building
skills.description: Building worlds with code - parts, models and pivots, materials, Lighting (LightingStyle, Atmosphere, post-processing), day/night, Terrain API, in-game CSG and destruction (GeometryService Subtract/Union/Fragment), ProceduralModel, EditableMesh/EditableImage, particles/beams/trails/highlights. Use when creating maps, environments, lighting, destructible objects, procedural levels, or visual effects.
skills.body:
# World building with code

## Parts and models

```luau
--!strict
local function makePart(size: Vector3, cframe: CFrame, props: { [string]: any }?): Part
	local part = Instance.new("Part")
	part.Anchored = true
	part.Size = size
	part.CFrame = cframe
	part.TopSurface = Enum.SurfaceType.Smooth
	part.BottomSurface = Enum.SurfaceType.Smooth
	for key, value in props or {} do
		(part :: any)[key] = value
	end
	return part -- caller sets Parent last
end

local floor = makePart(Vector3.new(64, 1, 64), CFrame.new(0, 0, 0), {
	Material = Enum.Material.Slate,
	Color = Color3.fromRGB(90, 90, 100),
})
local model = Instance.new("Model")
model.Name = "Arena"
floor.Parent = model
model.WorldPivot = floor.CFrame
model.Parent = workspace
model:PivotTo(CFrame.new(0, 10, 0) * CFrame.Angles(0, math.rad(45), 0))
```

- Set properties first, **parent last** (one replication/physics insert). Anchor static geometry.
- Move/rotate models with `PivotTo`/`GetPivot`; `Model.WorldPivot` / `PrimaryPart` define the pivot.
- Group logically related parts in Models (streaming, LOD, `ModelStreamingMode`), not giant containers.
- Decorative parts: `CanCollide/CanTouch/CanQuery = false`, `CastShadow = false` for tiny details.
- Materials: `Enum.Material.*`; custom looks via `MaterialVariant` in `MaterialService` (set
  `part.MaterialVariant = "Name"`) or `SurfaceAppearance` on MeshParts (PBR). `Decal.Texture` is
  superseded by `ColorMapContent`.
- Many identical meshes are cheap (instanced); many unique meshes/unions are not.

## Lighting

| Property | Guidance |
| --- | --- |
| `Lighting.LightingStyle` | `Realistic` (naturalistic) or `Soft` (stylized). Replaces the superseded `Lighting.Technology`. |
| `Lighting.PrioritizeLightingQuality` | Prefer quality (e.g. shadow maps with Soft) vs performance on lower-end devices. |
| `ClockTime` / `GeographicLatitude` | Sun position; animate `ClockTime` for day/night. |
| `Brightness`, `ExposureCompensation`, `Ambient`/`OutdoorAmbient` | Overall exposure and fill light. |
| `EnvironmentDiffuseScale`/`EnvironmentSpecularScale` | Skybox contribution to lighting and reflections. |
| Children | `Atmosphere` (haze/density, replaces fog), `Sky`, `Clouds` (in Terrain), `BloomEffect`, `ColorCorrectionEffect`, `ColorGradingEffect`, `DepthOfFieldEffect`, `SunRaysEffect`, `BlurEffect`. |

```luau
--!strict
-- Server: smooth day/night cycle (one full day every 20 minutes).
local Lighting = game:GetService("Lighting")
local RunService = game:GetService("RunService")

local DAY_LENGTH_SECONDS = 20 * 60

RunService.Heartbeat:Connect(function(deltaTime)
	Lighting.ClockTime = (Lighting.ClockTime + deltaTime * 24 / DAY_LENGTH_SECONDS) % 24
end)
```

For per-frame visual changes, prefer computing `ClockTime` on each client from
`workspace:GetServerTimeNow()` (no replication traffic, perfectly smooth). Local lights: `PointLight`,
`SpotLight`, `SurfaceLight` — few with `Shadows = true`.

## Terrain

```luau
--!strict
local terrain = workspace.Terrain

terrain:FillBlock(CFrame.new(0, -10, 0), Vector3.new(512, 20, 512), Enum.Material.Grass)
terrain:FillBall(Vector3.new(0, 0, 0), 24, Enum.Material.Air) -- carve a crater
terrain:FillBlock(CFrame.new(40, -2, 0), Vector3.new(30, 4, 30), Enum.Material.Water)
terrain:FillCylinder(CFrame.new(-40, 5, 0), 20, 8, Enum.Material.Rock)
```

- Bulk generation: build a `Region3` (aligned with `:ExpandToGrid(4)`) and use `ReadVoxels`/`WriteVoxels`
  with materials/occupancy arrays (4-stud voxels), in chunks, yielding between chunks.
- `terrain:Clear()`; water look via `Terrain.WaterColor`, `WaterWaveSize`, etc.
- **Custom terrain materials** (fully launched): up to 62 custom materials painted onto terrain, plus smaller
  files and faster loads. Opt in per place: Workspace → **Expanded Terrain = Enabled**, save, reopen; manage
  them in Window → 3D → Terrain Materials Manager. Thin terrain can show LOD gaps — keep it thick.
- Procedural heightmaps: sample `math.noise(x * scale, z * scale, seed)` with octaves; use a `Random.new(seed)`
  for deterministic worlds; generate on the server or use Parallel Luau for heavy math.

## In-game solid modeling and destruction (GeometryService)

```luau
--!strict
local GeometryService = game:GetService("GeometryService")

-- Punch a hole through a wall (e.g. explosions, building games).
local function carve(wall: BasePart, cutter: BasePart): { Instance }?
	local ok, results = pcall(function()
		return GeometryService:SubtractAsync(wall, { cutter }, {
			CollisionFidelity = Enum.CollisionFidelity.Default,
			RenderFidelity = Enum.RenderFidelity.Automatic,
			SplitApart = true, -- disconnected pieces become separate parts
		})
	end)
	if not ok or not results then
		return nil
	end
	for _, piece in results do
		if piece:IsA("BasePart") then
			piece.Anchored = wall.Anchored
			piece.Parent = wall.Parent
		end
	end
	wall:Destroy()
	return results
end

return carve
```

- `UnionAsync`, `IntersectAsync`, `SubtractAsync` return new unparented parts; `FragmentAsync(part, sites)`
  shatters a part (Voronoi) using points from `GenerateFragmentSites`; `SweepPartAsync` extrudes a part
  along CFrames; `CalculateConstraintsToPreserve` keeps welds/constraints when replacing parts.
- Operations are expensive: run on the server, rate-limit, and pool/clean up fragments.

## ProceduralModel (parameter-driven models)

`ProceduralModel` instances regenerate their contents from a **generator ModuleScript** exposing
`Attributes` (parameters) and `OnGenerate(params, targetContainer)`; works at edit time (undo/redo,
Team Create) and runtime. Generate from Studio, Assistant, or the Studio MCP (`generate_procedural_model`).
Creator Store procedural models are sandboxed automatically.

## Runtime meshes and images

`AssetService:CreateEditableMesh()` / `CreateEditableMeshAsync(content)` and `CreateEditableImage` enable
runtime geometry and pixel editing (deformable terrain chunks, painting, custom avatars). Published games
require the owner to be ID + 13+ verified and **Enable Mesh / Image APIs** in Creator Dashboard; strict
client memory budgets apply; only assets owned by/shared with the game owner can be loaded. Display via
`AssetService:CreateMeshPartAsync(Content.fromObject(editableMesh))`. For many vertices/faces use the
EditableMesh **batch APIs** and parallel queries (released for live games) instead of per-element calls.
Players can publish an `EditableImage` to their inventory from the server with
`AssetService:PromptCreatePlatformContentAsync(player, image, Enum.AssetType.Image)` (`pcall`; replaces
`PromptCreateAssetAsync`; needs a published place).

## Effects

- `ParticleEmitter` (use `:Emit(n)` for bursts), `Beam` (between attachments; lasers, ropes), `Trail`
  (swords, projectiles), `Highlight` (outline/fill; limited count), `Explosion` (sets off physics —
  set `DestroyJointRadiusPercent = 0` and `BlastPressure = 0` for visual-only).
- Spawn cosmetic effects on clients; destroy or pool them (`Debris:AddItem(obj, seconds)` is fine).

## Related skills

`roblox-performance` (rendering cost, streaming), `roblox-architecture` (streaming settings),
`roblox-studio-mcp` (build in Studio through MCP), `roblox-physics` (constraints, destruction physics).

skills.name: gh-fb-blender-web-pipeline
skills.description: Blender to web export workflows for 3D models and animations. Use this skill when exporting Blender models to glTF for web, optimizing 3D assets for Three.js or Babylon.js, batch processing models with Python scripts, automating Blender workflows, or creating web-ready 3D pipelines. Triggers on tasks involving Blender glTF export, bpy scripting, 3D asset optimization, model compression, texture baking, or Blender automation. Exports models for threejs-webgl, react-three-fiber, and babylonjs-engine skills.
skills.body:
# Blender Web Pipeline

## Overview

Blender Web Pipeline skill provides workflows for exporting 3D models and animations from Blender to web-optimized formats (primarily glTF 2.0). It covers Python scripting for batch processing, optimization techniques for web performance, and integration with web 3D libraries like Three.js and Babylon.js.

**When to use this skill:**
- Exporting Blender models for web applications
- Batch processing multiple 3D assets
- Optimizing file sizes for web delivery
- Automating repetitive Blender tasks
- Creating production pipelines for 3D web content
- Converting legacy formats to glTF

**Key capabilities:**
- glTF 2.0 export with optimization
- Python (bpy) automation scripts
- Texture baking and compression
- LOD (Level of Detail) generation
- Batch processing workflows
- Material and lighting optimization for web

## Core Concepts

### glTF 2.0 Format

**Why glTF for Web:**
- Industry-standard 3D format for web
- Efficient binary encoding (.glb)
- PBR materials support
- Animation and skinning
- Extensible with custom data
- Wide library support (Three.js, Babylon.js, etc.)

**glTF vs GLB:**
```
.gltf = JSON + external .bin + external textures
.glb  = Single binary file (recommended for web)
```

### Blender Python API (bpy)

**Access Blender data and operations via Python:**

```python
import bpy

# Access scene data
scene = bpy.context.scene
objects = bpy.data.objects

# Modify objects
obj = bpy.data.objects['Cube']
obj.location = (0, 0, 1)
obj.scale = (2, 2, 2)

# Export glTF
bpy.ops.export_scene.gltf(
    filepath='/path/to/model.glb',
    export_format='GLB'
)
```

### Web Optimization Goals

**Target Metrics:**
- File size: <5 MB per model (ideal <1 MB)
- Polygon count: <50k triangles for real-time
- Texture resolution: 2048x2048 max (1024x1024 preferred)
- Draw calls: Minimize via texture atlases
- Load time: <2 seconds on average connection

## Common Patterns

### 1. Basic glTF Export (Manual)

```python
# Blender Python Console or script

import bpy

# Select objects to export (optional - exports all if none selected)
bpy.ops.object.select_all(action='DESELECT')
bpy.data.objects['MyModel'].select_set(True)

# Export as GLB
bpy.ops.export_scene.gltf(
    filepath='/path/to/output.glb',
    export_format='GLB',                # Binary format
    use_selection=True,                 # Export selected only
    export_apply=True,                  # Apply modifiers
    export_texcoords=True,              # UV coordinates
    export_normals=True,                # Normals
    export_materials='EXPORT',          # Export materials
    export_colors=True,                 # Vertex colors
    export_cameras=False,               # Skip cameras
    export_lights=False,                # Skip lights
    export_animations=True,             # Include animations
    export_draco_mesh_compression_enable=True,  # Compress geometry
    export_draco_mesh_compression_level=6,      # 0-10 (6 recommended)
    export_draco_position_quantization=14,      # 8-14 bits
    export_draco_normal_quantization=10,        # 8-10 bits
    export_draco_texcoord_quantization=12       # 8-12 bits
)
```

### 2. Python Script for Batch Export

```python
#!/usr/bin/env blender --background --python
"""
Batch export all .blend files in a directory to glTF
Usage: blender --background --python batch_export.py -- /path/to/blend/files
"""

import bpy
import os
import sys

# Get command line arguments after --
argv = sys.argv
argv = argv[argv.index("--") + 1:] if "--" in argv else []

input_dir = argv[0] if argv else "/path/to/models"
output_dir = argv[1] if len(argv) > 1 else input_dir + "_gltf"

# Create output directory
os.makedirs(output_dir, exist_ok=True)

# Find all .blend files
blend_files = [f for f in os.listdir(input_dir) if f.endswith('.blend')]

print(f"Found {len(blend_files)} .blend files")

for blend_file in blend_files:
    input_path = os.path.join(input_dir, blend_file)
    output_name = blend_file.replace('.blend', '.glb')
    output_path = os.path.join(output_dir, output_name)

    print(f"Processing: {blend_file}")

    # Open blend file
    bpy.ops.wm.open_mainfile(filepath=input_path)

    # Export as GLB with optimizations
    bpy.ops.export_scene.gltf(
        filepath=output_path,
        export_format='GLB',
        export_apply=True,
        export_draco_mesh_compression_enable=True,
        export_draco_mesh_compression_level=6
    )

    print(f"  Exported: {output_name}")

print("Batch export complete!")
```

**Run batch script:**

```bash
blender --background --python batch_export.py -- /models/source /models/output
```

### 3. Optimize Model for Web (Decimation)

```python
import bpy

def optimize_mesh(obj, target_ratio=0.5):
    """Reduce polygon count using decimation modifier."""

    if obj.type != 'MESH':
        return

    # Add Decimate modifier
    decimate = obj.modifiers.new(name='Decimate', type='DECIMATE')
    decimate.ratio = target_ratio  # 0.5 = 50% of original polygons
    decimate.use_collapse_triangulate = True

    # Apply modifier
    bpy.context.view_layer.objects.active = obj
    bpy.ops.object.modifier_apply(modifier='Decimate')

    print(f"Optimized {obj.name}: {len(obj.data.polygons)} polygons")

# Optimize all selected meshes
for obj in bpy.context.selected_objects:
    optimize_mesh(obj, target_ratio=0.3)
```

### 4. Texture Baking for Web

```python
import bpy

def bake_textures(obj, resolution=1024):
    """Bake all materials to single texture."""

    # Setup bake settings
    bpy.context.scene.render.engine = 'CYCLES'
    bpy.context.scene.cycles.bake_type = 'COMBINED'

    # Create bake image
    bake_image = bpy.data.images.new(
        name=f"{obj.name}_bake",
        width=resolution,
        height=resolution
    )

    # Create bake material
    mat = bpy.data.materials.new(name=f"{obj.name}_baked")
    mat.use_nodes = True
    nodes = mat.node_tree.nodes

    # Add Image Texture node
    tex_node = nodes.new(type='ShaderNodeTexImage')
    tex_node.image = bake_image
    tex_node.select = True
    nodes.active = tex_node

    # Assign material
    if obj.data.materials:
        obj.data.materials[0] = mat
    else:
        obj.data.materials.append(mat)

    # Select object
    bpy.context.view_layer.objects.active = obj
    obj.select_set(True)

    # Bake
    bpy.ops.object.bake(type='COMBINED')

    # Save baked texture
    bake_image.filepath_raw = f"/tmp/{obj.name}_bake.png"
    bake_image.file_format = 'PNG'
    bake_image.save()

    print(f"Baked {obj.name} to {bake_image.filepath_raw}")

# Bake selected objects
for obj in bpy.context.selected_objects:
    if obj.type == 'MESH':
        bake_textures(obj, resolution=2048)
```

### 5. Generate LOD (Level of Detail)

```python
import bpy

def generate_lods(obj, lod_levels=[0.75, 0.5, 0.25]):
    """Generate LOD copies with decreasing polygon counts."""

    lod_objects = []

    for i, ratio in enumerate(lod_levels):
        # Duplicate object
        lod_obj = obj.copy()
        lod_obj.data = obj.data.copy()
        lod_obj.name = f"{obj.name}_LOD{i}"

        # Link to scene
        bpy.context.collection.objects.link(lod_obj)

        # Add Decimate modifier
        decimate = lod_obj.modifiers.new(name='Decimate', type='DECIMATE')
        decimate.ratio = ratio

        # Apply modifier
        bpy.context.view_layer.objects.active = lod_obj
        bpy.ops.object.modifier_apply(modifier='Decimate')

        lod_objects.append(lod_obj)

        print(f"Created {lod_obj.name}: {len(lod_obj.data.polygons)} polygons")

    return lod_objects

# Generate LODs for selected object
if bpy.context.active_object:
    generate_lods(bpy.context.active_object)
```

### 6. Export with Texture Compression

```python
import bpy
import os

def export_optimized_gltf(filepath, texture_max_size=1024):
    """Export glTF with downscaled textures."""

    # Downscale all textures
    for img in bpy.data.images:
        if img.size[0] > texture_max_size or img.size[1] > texture_max_size:
            img.scale(texture_max_size, texture_max_size)
            print(f"Downscaled {img.name} to {texture_max_size}x{texture_max_size}")

    # Export with Draco compression
    bpy.ops.export_scene.gltf(
        filepath=filepath,
        export_format='GLB',
        export_apply=True,
        export_image_format='JPEG',  # JPEG for smaller size (or PNG for quality)
        export_jpeg_quality=85,       # 0-100
        export_draco_mesh_compression_enable=True,
        export_draco_mesh_compression_level=8,  # Max compression
        export_draco_position_quantization=12,
        export_draco_normal_quantization=8,
        export_draco_texcoord_quantization=10
    )

# Export optimized
export_optimized_gltf('/path/to/optimized.glb', texture_max_size=512)
```

### 7. Command-Line Automation

```bash
#!/bin/bash
# Batch export Blender files to glTF without opening GUI

SCRIPT_DIR="$(dirname "$0")"

# Export all .blend files in current directory
for blend_file in *.blend; do
    echo "Exporting $blend_file..."

    blender --background "$blend_file" --python - <<EOF
import bpy
import os

# Get output filename
filename = os.path.splitext(bpy.data.filepath)[0]
output = filename + '.glb'

# Export
bpy.ops.export_scene.gltf(
    filepath=output,
    export_format='GLB',
    export_apply=True,
    export_draco_mesh_compression_enable=True,
    export_draco_mesh_compression_level=6
)

print(f'Exported to {output}')
EOF

done

echo "All files exported!"
```

## Integration Patterns

### With Three.js

```javascript
import * as THREE from 'three';
import { GLTFLoader } from 'three/addons/loaders/GLTFLoader.js';
import { DRACOLoader } from 'three/addons/loaders/DRACOLoader.js';

const loader = new GLTFLoader();

// Setup Draco decoder for compressed models
const dracoLoader = new DRACOLoader();
dracoLoader.setDecoderPath('/draco/');
loader.setDRACOLoader(dracoLoader);

// Load Blender export
loader.load('/models/exported.glb', (gltf) => {
  scene.add(gltf.scene);

  // Play animations
  if (gltf.animations.length > 0) {
    const mixer = new THREE.AnimationMixer(gltf.scene);
    const action = mixer.clipAction(gltf.animations[0]);
    action.play();
  }
});
```

### With React Three Fiber

```jsx
import { useGLTF } from '@react-three/drei';

function Model() {
  const { scene } = useGLTF('/models/exported.glb');
  return <primitive object={scene} />;
}

// Preload for better performance
useGLTF.preload('/models/exported.glb');
```

### With Babylon.js

```javascript
import * as BABYLON from '@babylonjs/core';
import '@babylonjs/loaders/glTF';

BABYLON.SceneLoader.ImportMesh(
  '',
  '/models/',
  'exported.glb',
  scene,
  (meshes) => {
    console.log('Loaded meshes:', meshes);
  }
);
```

## Optimization Techniques

### 1. Geometry Optimization

**Decimate Modifier:**
```python
# Reduce polygon count by 70%
obj.modifiers.new(name='Decimate', type='DECIMATE')
obj.modifiers['Decimate'].ratio = 0.3
```

**Merge by Distance:**
```python
# Remove duplicate vertices
bpy.ops.object.mode_set(mode='EDIT')
bpy.ops.mesh.select_all(action='SELECT')
bpy.ops.mesh.remove_doubles(threshold=0.0001)
bpy.ops.object.mode_set(mode='OBJECT')
```

**Triangulate Faces:**
```python
# Ensure all faces are triangles (required for some engines)
bpy.ops.object.mode_set(mode='EDIT')
bpy.ops.mesh.select_all(action='SELECT')
bpy.ops.mesh.quads_convert_to_tris()
bpy.ops.object.mode_set(mode='OBJECT')
```

### 2. Texture Optimization

**Image Compression:**
```python
# Save textures as JPEG (lossy but smaller)
for img in bpy.data.images:
    img.file_format = 'JPEG'
    img.filepath_raw = f"/output/{img.name}.jpg"
    img.save()
```

**Texture Atlas:**
```python
# Combine multiple textures into one atlas
# Use Smart UV Project for automatic atlasing
bpy.ops.object.mode_set(mode='EDIT')
bpy.ops.mesh.select_all(action='SELECT')
bpy.ops.uv.smart_project(angle_limit=66, island_margin=0.02)
bpy.ops.object.mode_set(mode='OBJECT')
```

### 3. Material Simplification

**Convert to PBR:**
```python
# Ensure materials use Principled BSDF (glTF standard)
for mat in bpy.data.materials:
    if not mat.use_nodes:
        mat.use_nodes = True

    nodes = mat.node_tree.nodes
    principled = nodes.get('Principled BSDF')

    if not principled:
        principled = nodes.new(type='ShaderNodeBsdfPrincipled')
        output = nodes.get('Material Output')
        mat.node_tree.links.new(principled.outputs[0], output.inputs[0])
```

## Common Pitfalls

### 1. Large File Sizes

**Problem:** Exported .glb files are 20+ MB

**Solutions:**
- Enable Draco compression (60-90% reduction)
- Reduce texture resolution (2048 → 1024 or 512)
- Use JPEG instead of PNG for textures
- Decimate geometry (target <50k triangles)
- Remove unused materials/textures

### 2. Missing Textures in Export

**Problem:** Textures don't appear in web viewer

**Solutions:**
- Ensure all images are saved (not packed)
- Use relative paths for textures
- Export with "Export Images" enabled
- Check image format compatibility (PNG/JPEG)

### 3. Animations Not Playing

**Problem:** Animations don't export or play incorrectly

**Solutions:**
- Ensure animations are on timeline (not NLA strips)
- Export with "Export Animations" enabled
- Check animation actions are assigned to objects
- Use "Bake Actions" for complex rigs

### 4. Materials Look Different

**Problem:** Materials render differently in web vs Blender

**Solutions:**
- Use Principled BSDF (maps to glTF PBR)
- Avoid custom shader nodes (won't export)
- Use supported texture types (Base Color, Metallic, Roughness, Normal, Emission)
- Test in glTF viewer before deploying

### 5. Slow Export Times

**Problem:** Export takes 10+ minutes

**Solutions:**
- Apply modifiers before export (don't export non-destructively)
- Reduce geometry complexity
- Remove unused data (orphan cleanup)
- Use command-line export (faster than GUI)

### 6. Performance Issues in Browser

**Problem:** Model lags in browser

**Solutions:**
- Generate LODs (Level of Detail)
- Use instancing for repeated objects
- Limit draw calls (merge objects, texture atlases)
- Reduce polygon count (<50k triangles)
- Optimize shaders (avoid transparency/refraction)

## Best Practices

### Pre-Export Checklist

```
☐ Apply all modifiers
☐ Merge vertices (remove doubles)
☐ Triangulate faces (if required)
☐ Optimize polygon count (<50k triangles)
☐ UV unwrap all meshes
☐ Bake materials (if complex)
☐ Resize textures (max 2048x2048)
☐ Use Principled BSDF materials
☐ Remove unused data (orphan cleanup)
☐ Name objects descriptively
☐ Set origin points correctly
☐ Apply transformations (Ctrl+A)
```

### Export Settings

```python
# Recommended glTF export settings
bpy.ops.export_scene.gltf(
    filepath='/output.glb',
    export_format='GLB',                # Binary format
    export_apply=True,                  # Apply modifiers
    export_image_format='JPEG',         # Smaller file size
    export_jpeg_quality=85,             # Quality vs size
    export_draco_mesh_compression_enable=True,  # Enable compression
    export_draco_mesh_compression_level=6,      # Balance speed/size
    export_animations=True,             # Include animations
    export_lights=False,                # Skip lights (recreate in code)
    export_cameras=False                # Skip cameras
)
```

skills.description: Plans, generates or sources, and validates consistent game art: style guides, sprites, pixel art, tilesets, icons and textures, with QA and licence records. Use when making or AI-generating game art, fixing fake transparency, or checking Steam AI disclosure. Not for engine import (`godot-tilemap`, `godot-animation`, `unity-tilemap-2d`), UI layout (`game-ui-ux`) or sound (`audio-design`).
skills.body:
# Create Game Assets

Turn a game's visual intent into a consistent, engine-ready asset set. Treat image generation as
one production tool inside a controlled pipeline, never as proof that an asset is shippable.

## When to use

- Defining or refreshing an art direction, or writing a style guide other contributors follow.
- Producing a family of sprites, tiles, icons, backgrounds or textures that must match.
- Generating art with an image tool, or sourcing licensed packs, and making the result usable.
- Auditing what was generated or licensed before release.

**Not this skill:** importing into the engine (`godot-tilemap`, `unity-tilemap-2d`,
`pixijs-rendering`, `threejs-gltf-loading`), animating the sprites (`godot-animation`,
`unity-animation`), atlas and texture-memory budgets at runtime (`performance-optimization`).

## Core workflow

1. **Inspect before inventing.** Find existing screenshots, concept art, sprites, models, fonts,
   import settings, camera framing, target resolution, and naming conventions. Preserve a coherent
   existing direction unless the user asks for a redesign.
2. **Lock the technical frame.** Record engine, 2D/3D, camera/view, native display size, asset
   dimensions, world scale, transparency, palette, filtering, animation frames, texture budget,
   and target platforms. Use `assets/art-direction-brief.md` as a copyable brief.
3. **Name the visual system.** Define shape language, silhouette priorities, value structure,
   palette roles, materials, lighting, detail density, edge treatment, and motion character. Use
   concrete visual properties; do not substitute a living artist's name for an art direction.
4. **Make an asset manifest.** Copy `assets/asset-manifest.json`, then list every required asset,
   state, variant, size, pivot, collision role, source, license, and approval status. Separate
   production assets from disposable greybox placeholders.
5. **Approve one visual target.** Create or select a representative hero asset or small style
   board before producing a full set. Judge it at actual game scale and against a gameplay
   background. If the user delegated the choice, pick the strongest viable direction and record
   the decision instead of blocking.
6. **Produce related assets as families.** Reuse the approved target as an edit/reference input.
   Keep palette, view, proportions, lighting, outline, and texture density invariant. Generate
   small coherent batches; avoid unrelated one-off prompts that drift.
7. **Normalize deterministically.** Crop, size, anchor, slice, name, compress, and check alpha with
   ordinary image/DCC tools. Never trust generated grids, transparency, seams, pivots, topology,
   or dimensions without inspection. Use the bundled scripts for raster QA and contact sheets.
8. **Import with engine-native settings.** Set filtering, mipmaps, pixels-per-unit/world scale,
   color space, compression, sprite slicing, texture types, materials, and collision deliberately.
   Read the relevant engine skill before editing engine files.
9. **Validate in context.** Inspect a contact sheet and the actual game at native resolution.
   Check silhouette, scale, animation stability, seams, legibility, palette, collision fit, memory,
   and compression artifacts. Iterate on the source asset, not only on runtime compensations.
10. **Record provenance.** Keep the source URL/tool, license or generation note, edit history, and
    restrictions beside the manifest. Preserve embedded provenance metadata when the pipeline can.
11. **Finish with the checks.** Run `scripts/asset_report.py` over every file in the batch with
    the manifest's size, alpha and colour limits and `--json`; it must exit 0. Build a contact
    sheet with `scripts/build_preview_sheet.py` and look at it. Confirm every shipped manifest
    entry has a source, licence and `technical_checks_passed: true`. Then ask the user to view
    the assets in the running game at native resolution and report anything that does not read.

## Choose the production path

| Need | Default path |
|------|--------------|
| Existing asset needs a controlled change | Edit the original/reference; state what must remain unchanged |
| New 2D visual family | Approve seed → generate/source family → normalize → preview → import |
| True pixel art | Use generated work as a draft; enforce grid, palette, clusters, and frames with pixel tools |
| Tileable surface or tileset | Produce a small family; repair seams; test repeated 3×3 before approval |
| UI art or icons | Keep text and interaction code-native; prefer SVG/vector for simple geometric symbols |
| 3D model or material | Use concepts as reference; author/clean in a DCC; validate topology, UVs, scale, pivots, and LODs |
| No generation/edit tool is available | Build the brief and manifest; source licensed assets or keep explicit greybox placeholders |
| Audio asset | Route sound implementation and mixing to `audio-design`; still track source/license in the manifest |

## Image-generation handoff

When a capable image generation or editing tool is installed, use it for live visual creation. If
the workspace exposes an `imagegen` skill, read and follow it for the actual generation/edit call;
this skill owns the game-art brief, constraints, normalization, and acceptance gates. Generation
APIs usually bill per image: tell the user the batch size and ask before large or repeated runs.

Build prompts from these blocks:

```text
ROLE/PURPOSE: production asset for [gameplay role]
SUBJECT: [specific object/character and action]
VIEW: [orthographic/top-down/side/three-quarter], [camera and facing]
ART DIRECTION: [shape language], [palette roles], [materials], [edge treatment]
GAME-SCALE READ: [silhouette and focal details that must survive at WxH]
TECHNICAL OUTPUT: [dimensions/aspect], [transparent or scene background], [frame/slot count]
LOCKS: preserve [identity, proportions, palette, costume, lighting, line weight]
EXCLUDE: text, labels, mockup frames, scenery, duplicate objects, cropped edges, signatures
```

For edits, say both what changes and what stays fixed. Ask for transparent output through the
tool's native transparency option when available, then verify the alpha channel—prompt wording
alone does not guarantee transparency.

## Raster QA recipes

Inspect constraints and emit a machine-readable report. `--require-alpha` also fails an RGBA file
whose every pixel is opaque, which is how a baked background or fake checkerboard shows up:

```bash
python scripts/asset_report.py assets/player-idle.png \
  --expect-size 64x64 --require-alpha --max-colors 48 --json
```

Build a nearest-neighbor contact sheet over a checkerboard:

```bash
python scripts/build_preview_sheet.py output/player/*.png \
  --out output/player-preview.png --columns 4 --cell-size 192
```

Run script paths relative to this skill directory, or resolve the installed skill path first.
Both scripts need Python and Pillow (see Version notes). Install the only dependency with
`python -m pip install -r scripts/requirements.txt` when it is not already available.
`asset_report.py` exits 1 when any explicit constraint fails, so it can gate a build.

## Quality gates

- **Cohesion:** related assets share palette roles, line/edge treatment, view, light direction,
  scale, and detail density.
- **Gameplay read:** silhouettes and state changes remain clear at native resolution, in motion,
  and over real backgrounds.
- **Technical fit:** exact size/frame count, usable alpha, stable anchors/pivots, correct color
  space/filtering, no clipped content, no accidental labels or baked mockup chrome.
- **Animation:** identity, volume, proportions, costume, facing, and baseline do not drift; timing
  and anticipation read in an in-engine preview.
- **Tiles/backgrounds:** required edges tile without seams; repetition is tolerable; parallax
  layers have intentional depth and no baked collision cues.
- **3D:** transforms, scale, pivot, normals, UVs, materials, topology, rig, collision proxies,
  LODs, and runtime format are checked rather than inferred from a render.
- **Rights:** every shipped file has recorded provenance and terms compatible with the project.

Do not call an asset production-ready from a prompt result alone. Approval requires the relevant
technical checks plus an in-engine or native-scale visual inspection.

## Gotchas

- **Fake transparency.** Image models often paint a grey-and-white checkerboard or a flat
  backdrop instead of alpha. `asset_report.py --require-alpha` fails a file with no alpha
  channel or with every pixel opaque; remove the background with a real matte, never by trusting
  the prompt.
- **Halos around cut-outs.** Semi-transparent edges keep the old background colour and show as a
  light or dark fringe in the engine. Bleed edge colour outward into transparent pixels (or
  export premultiplied when the engine expects it) and check over a contrasting background.
- **Pseudo pixel art.** Generated "pixel art" has blended in-between colours, off-grid pixels and
  hundreds of near-duplicates. Downscale to the true grid with nearest-neighbour, quantize to
  the palette, then check `--max-colors`.
- **Mipmaps or linear filtering on pixel art** blur and shimmer it. Nearest filtering, no
  mipmaps, integer camera scale.
- **Sprite sheets that do not slice.** Generated grids drift by a few pixels per cell and frames
  change size. Re-slice onto a fixed canvas with one shared anchor (usually bottom-centre) before
  import.
- **Character drift between frames or batches** (head size, outline width, palette). Edit from
  the approved seed each time instead of from the last output.
- **Texture bleeding at tile and atlas edges** under zoom or mipmaps. Pad or extrude tiles by 1-2
  px and test a 3x3 repeat at the game's camera scale.
- **Block-compression sizes.** BC and ETC2 compress in 4x4 blocks (ASTC in its chosen block
  size); other dimensions get padded, or rejected by stricter paths such as WebGL compressed
  textures. Keep textures at multiples of 4, and powers of two where mipmaps are needed.
- **Normal and data maps imported as sRGB** shade wrongly. Only colour textures are sRGB.
- **Generated text and logos** come out as near-letters and invite trademark trouble. Keep text
  code-native and remove marks before approval.
- **Licences that do not survive packing.** Attribution and terms must follow the asset through
  atlases and renames; record them in the manifest, not in a filename.
- **Undeclared AI content.** Steam's Content Survey asks about AI-generated content that ships
  with the game; answer it from the manifest's `source.kind`, so record generation per asset.

## References

- For visual-system decisions and maintaining consistency, read
  `references/art-direction.md`.
- For sprites, animation strips, tiles, backgrounds, UI art, and engine import settings, read
  `references/raster-pipeline.md`.
- For concept-to-mesh, textures, glTF/GLB, LOD, collision, and runtime validation, read
  `references/three-d-pipeline.md`.
- For licenses, generated-media records, and provenance, read
  `references/provenance.md`.

## Related skills

- `game-ui-ux` for layout, navigation, readability, and accessible interaction.
- `game-feel`, `shader-programming`, and `audio-design` for presentation after the source art fits.
- Engine import/rendering skills such as `godot-tilemap`, `unity-tilemap-2d`,
  `pixijs-rendering`, and `threejs-gltf-loading`.

## Version notes

Last verified: 2026-11-11.

- Scripts: Python 3.10+ with Pillow 10 to 13 (`scripts/requirements.txt` pins `Pillow>=10,<14`).
  Pillow 13.0.0 is the latest release and requires Python 3.11+
  (https://pypi.org/project/pillow/).
- Steam Content Survey: the generative AI section separates pre-generated content (made during
  development and shipped) from live-generated content (made while the game runs, which also
  needs a description of guardrails); AI tools used only for efficiency are not its focus
  (https://partner.steamgames.com/doc/gettingstarted/contentsurvey).
- Engine import settings in `references/raster-pipeline.md` target Godot 4.7 and Unity 6.3 LTS.

skills.name: gh-gd-dialogue-systems
skills.description: Builds engine-neutral branching dialogue with Ink, Yarn Spinner or a small JSON graph runner: lines, choices, conditions, variables and localization IDs. Use for NPC conversations, dialogue trees, barks, .ink or .yarn files, or dialogue that dead-ends. Not for visual-novel backlog and skip (`visual-novel`), quests (`rpg`) or text box widgets (`godot-ui-control`, `game-ui-ux`).
skills.body:
# Dialogue systems

Model conversations as a graph: nodes hold lines, choices branch, conditions gate options and
a variable store remembers what the player did. The first decision is build or adopt: Ink or
Yarn Spinner when writers need real flow control, a small data-driven runner when lines,
choices and flags are enough. Never build a new scripting language.

## When to use

- Designing branching conversations, choice menus or narrative state that later lines read.
- Choosing between Ink, Yarn Spinner and a custom JSON/resource graph.
- Wiring a dialogue runtime into the game loop: advance, show choices, run commands, persist.

**Not this skill:** VN presentation and flow (`visual-novel`), quest logic (`rpg`), widget
code (`godot-ui-control`, `roblox-ui`) and UI layout rules (`game-ui-ux`), persisting variables
across sessions (`save-systems`).

## Core workflow

1. **Inspect the project**: existing `.ink`/`.yarn`/`.yarnproject` files, an installed
   integration (ink-unity-integration, inkjs, Yarn Spinner for Unity or Godot), or a JSON graph.
   Keep what exists.
2. **Choose the tool.**
   - **Ink**: prose-first, weave and gather flow, read counts as free flags; best for
     dialogue-heavy or choose-your-own-adventure narrative.
   - **Yarn Spinner**: node-based, explicit `<<commands>>` dispatched to game code, built-in
     line IDs for localization; best for game-driven dialogue with many engine hooks.
   - **Custom runner**: a JSON graph plus about 100 lines of interpreter, when you need full
     control or no dependency.
3. **Define the node contract**: a node yields a line (speaker plus line ID), a choice set, a
   command, or an end/jump. The runner hands lines and choices to the UI and waits.
4. **Keep variables outside the UI** in one store the dialogue reads and writes, so cutscenes,
   tests and saves see the same state.
5. **Author line IDs from day one**; display text comes from a per-locale string table.
6. **Apply costs on the transition** (the choice), not on a node the player can revisit.
7. **Validate before handing back:**
   - Ink: `inklecate -o story.json story.ink` exits 1 on compile errors.
   - Yarn: `ysc compile story.yarn` reports errors; `ysc run --auto-advance story.yarn` plays it
     in the terminal.
   - Custom graph: run `validate_graph()` from `references/runner.md`; it must return no
     problems (missing targets, nodes without an exit, undeclared variables, unreachable nodes).
   - Then walk each choice path once with a script that picks choices in order.

## Patterns

### 1. Engine-neutral dialogue graph (data, not code)

```json
{
  "start": "guard_intro",
  "vars": { "gold": 0, "gate_open": false },
  "nodes": {
    "guard_intro": {
      "speaker": "Guard", "line": "DLG_GUARD_001",
      "choices": [
        { "text": "DLG_OPT_BRIBE", "to": "bribe", "if": "gold >= 50",
          "set": { "gold": "gold - 50" } },
        { "text": "DLG_OPT_LEAVE", "to": "end" }
      ]
    },
    "bribe": {
      "speaker": "Guard", "line": "DLG_GUARD_BRIBED",
      "set": { "gate_open": true },
      "next": "end"
    },
    "end": { "end": true }
  }
}
```

`line`/`text` are **string-table IDs** (localization), not literal text. `if`
gates a choice; `set` mutates the variable store. The gold cost sits on the
*choice*, so it is paid once per pick even if the `bribe` node is revisited; the
idempotent `gate_open` write can live on the node. A string `set` value is an
expression, so a literal string needs inner quotes: `"mood": "'angry'"`. The full
interpreter that walks this graph is in `references/runner.md`. Its variable store
starts from `vars`; replace those defaults with the player's saved narrative state
when starting a real conversation. Declare every referenced variable so unknown
names still expose authoring mistakes.

### 2. Runner step (a state machine over the graph)

```gdscript
# Godot 4.7. The runner holds the current node and a variable store. Every line
# waits for the player: the UI calls choose() or the continue callback.
func goto(id: String) -> void:
    current = graph.nodes[id]
    apply_set(current.get("set", {}))
    if current.get("end", false):
        ui.close()
        return
    if current.has("line"):
        ui.show_line(current.get("speaker", ""), localize(current.line))
    if current.has("choices"):
        var shown = current.choices.filter(func(c): return eval_cond(c.get("if", "")))
        ui.show_choices(shown)            # only choices whose condition passes
    elif current.has("next"):
        var next_id: String = current.next
        ui.show_continue(func(): goto(next_id))   # advance when the player continues

func choose(choice: Dictionary) -> void:   # called when the player picks a choice
    apply_set(choice.get("set", {}))       # write on the transition (revisit-safe)
    goto(choice.to)
```

### 3. Ink — branching with knots, choices, and variables (inkle)

```ink
// Ink: '*' = once-only choice, '+' = sticky. [bracketed] text shows only in the
// choice, not the printed result. '->' diverts; '-> END' stops the flow.
VAR gold = 60
-> guard_intro                    // the story starts at the top: divert into a knot

=== guard_intro ===
The guard blocks the gate.
* {gold >= 50} [Offer 50 gold]   "Here, take it."
    ~ gold = gold - 50
    The guard pockets it and steps aside. -> END
* [Leave]   You turn back. -> END
```

Ink tracks how often each knot was seen, so `{visited_knot}` is a built-in
condition. Variables are global (`VAR`) or temporary (`~ temp`).

### 4. Yarn Spinner — nodes, options, and commands (Yarn Spinner 3.x)

```yarn
title: GuardIntro
---
<<declare $gold = 60>>
<<declare $gate_open = false>>
Guard: You can't pass.
-> Offer 50 gold <<if $gold >= 50>>
    <<set $gold = $gold - 50>>
    Guard: ...fine. Go on through.
    <<set $gate_open to true>>
-> Leave
    Guard: Good choice.
===
```

Yarn lines may start with `Speaker:`; options use `->`; `<<set>>`/`<<declare>>`
manage `$variables`; `<<if>>` gates an option; `<<jump NodeName>>` moves between
nodes. Interpolate values in text with `{$gold}`. Declare every variable before first
use: an undeclared one still compiles (Yarn infers its type and a zero/false/empty
start value) with only a warning, which hides typos. These constructs are unchanged from
Yarn Spinner 2.x.

## Gotchas

- **Display strings in the script** instead of line IDs turn localization into a rewrite.
  Yarn tags lines with `#line:` IDs (`ysc tag` adds them); Ink has no line IDs, so tag lines
  yourself (`#id:guard_01`) or translate whole files.
- **A cost on a revisitable node** (`gold - 50` on `bribe`) is paid again on every visit. Put it
  on the choice, or guard it with a seen-flag.
- **Ink `*` versus `+`.** `*` choices vanish after one use, so a looping hub menu built from `*`
  empties itself. Hub menus use sticky `+`.
- **Ink choice text printed twice or not at all.** Text inside `[brackets]` shows only in the
  choice; text before them shows in both; text after only in the output.
- **Ink runtime loop stops after a choice.** After `ChooseChoiceIndex(i)` call `Continue()` (or
  `ContinueMaximally()`) again; the chosen branch prints nothing until you do.
- **Yarn undeclared variables compile with only a warning** and start at 0, false or "", which
  hides typos. `<<declare>>` everything.
- **Yarn 3 syntax in a Yarn 2 project** (`<<once>>`, `<<detour>>`, `when:` node groups) fails
  with "requires version 3 or later". Check the `.yarnproject` language version.
- **Ink Unity integration 2.0** imports `.ink` as an `InkFile` asset; code that loaded the old
  generated `.json` `TextAsset` must switch to `new Story(inkFile.storyJson)`.
- **Dead ends** (a node with no next, choices or end) silently stall the conversation. The
  validation step catches them.
- **`eval()` on dialogue expressions** runs arbitrary code from data files and mods. Use a
  whitelisting evaluator (the runner's `evaluate`).

## References

- `references/ink-and-yarn.md`: read when writing or reviewing `.ink` or `.yarn` (side-by-side
  syntax, Ink weave features, Yarn 3 additions, runtime integration and localization).
- `references/runner.md`: read when building or fixing a custom runner (schema, sandboxed
  `evaluate`, `DialogueRunner`, localization lookup, `validate_graph`).

## Related skills

- `save-systems`: persist narrative variables and seen-flags.
- `godot-resources`, `unity-scriptableobjects`: store dialogue as engine data.
- `godot-ui-control`, `game-ui-ux`: text boxes, portraits and choice buttons.
- `visual-novel`, `rpg`: genres that compose this skill.

## Version notes

Last verified: 2026-11-11.

- Ink 1.2.1 (May 2026) with ink-unity-integration 2.0.0 (July 2026); `inklecate` exits with code
  1 on compile errors and defaults its output to `<name>.ink.json`
  (https://github.com/inkle/ink/releases, inklecate `CommandLineTool.cs`).
- Yarn Spinner 3.2.1 compiler (May 2026), Yarn Spinner for Unity 3.2.8 (August 2026), `ysc`
  3.2.2 with `compile`, `run`, `tag` and `extract`
  (https://github.com/YarnSpinnerTool/YarnSpinner-Console).
- Yarn Spinner engine status: Unity stable; Godot GDScript edition in Early Access (3.3 docs,
  Godot 4.6 or later, not yet recommended for shipping); Godot C# edition marked
  work-in-progress without official support; Unreal listed as a pre-release for UE 5.7 or later
  (https://yarnspinner.dev, https://github.com/YarnSpinnerTool/YarnSpinner-Godot-GDScript,
  https://github.com/YarnSpinnerTool/YarnSpinner-Godot).

skills.name: gh-gd-procedural-gen
skills.description: Engine-neutral procedural generation in Python with Godot and Unity mappings: seeded RNG, dungeon layouts, wave function collapse, noise terrain and loot tables. Use for a dungeon generator, WFC or Perlin terrain, or seeds that give different maps. Not for roguelike run structure (`roguelike`), deckbuilders (`card-game`) or painting tiles (`godot-tilemap`, `unity-tilemap-2d`).
skills.body:
# Procedural generation

Generate levels, terrain and drops from rules and a seed. The property that matters most is
**determinism**: one seed reproduces one world, so bugs replay and players can share seeds.
This skill owns the algorithms and their validation; genre skills such as `roguelike` and
`survival-crafting` decide what to generate and when.

## When to use

- Map, dungeon, cave, terrain or item-drop generators, in any engine.
- Results that must reproduce from a seed (debugging, daily challenges, shareable worlds).
- Validating generated content: reachable rooms, a safe spawn, a path to the exit, no key behind
  its own lock.

**Not this skill:** run structure, permadeath and meta-progression (`roguelike`), deck and card
pools (`card-game`), drawing tiles (`godot-tilemap`, `unity-tilemap-2d`), pathfinding over the
result (`game-ai`), hand-paced levels (`level-design`).

## Core workflow

1. **Own the randomness.** Create one seeded RNG and pass it to every function that makes a
   choice. Global random calls make results depend on call order and on other systems.
2. **Pick the technique for the content.** Continuous terrain: noise. Rooms and corridors: BSP
   or placement plus a spanning tree. Caves: random walk or cellular automata. Tile adjacency
   rules: WFC. Rarities: weighted tables.
3. **Generate into plain data** (a grid of ints, a list of rooms), separate from rendering, so it
   can be tested without the engine.
4. **Validate every result**: flood-fill connectivity from the spawn, spawn safety, a path to the
   exit, key order. Reject and regenerate with a derived seed, or repair.
5. **Tune with the seed fixed** so each parameter change is visible, then sweep many seeds to
   check the distribution and the failure rate.
6. **Run the seed sweep** (Pattern 4) and report its numbers.

## Patterns

### 1. Seeded RNG

```python
import random
rng = random.Random(seed)        # a dedicated instance, never the module-level random.*
room_count = rng.randint(5, 12)
sub = random.Random(rng.getrandbits(64))   # derive a child stream per system or per chunk
```

Engine equivalents: Godot 4.7 `var rng := RandomNumberGenerator.new(); rng.seed = s` (save
`rng.state` to resume mid-sequence); Unity `new Unity.Mathematics.Random(seed)` (a non-zero
`uint`) or `new System.Random(seed)`. Avoid `UnityEngine.Random.InitState` for generation: it
seeds the one global generator every other script also draws from. Derive child seeds per
system (layout, loot, decoration) so adding a decoration roll does not reshuffle the layout.

### 2. A PRNG whose sequence you own

```python
class SplitMix64:
    """Tiny PRNG whose sequence you own: same seed, same numbers, on every version."""
    MASK = (1 << 64) - 1

    def __init__(self, seed: int):
        self.state = seed & self.MASK

    def next_u64(self) -> int:
        self.state = (self.state + 0x9E3779B97F4A7C15) & self.MASK
        z = self.state
        z = ((z ^ (z >> 30)) * 0xBF58476D1CE4E5B9) & self.MASK
        z = ((z ^ (z >> 27)) * 0x94D049BB133111EB) & self.MASK
        return z ^ (z >> 31)

    def below(self, n: int) -> int:            # 0 <= result < n, without modulo bias
        limit = self.MASK - (self.MASK + 1) % n
        while (x := self.next_u64()) > limit:
            pass
        return x % n

# Pin the first outputs in a test so a refactor cannot change every shared seed.
rng = SplitMix64(0)
assert [rng.next_u64() for _ in range(3)] == [
    0xE220A8397B1DCDAF, 0x6E789E6AA1B965F4, 0x06C45D188009454F]
```

Use it when seeds must survive engine, runtime or library updates (daily challenges, seed-only
saves, cross-platform shared seeds). Port the same arithmetic to C# with `ulong` or to GDScript
with care: GDScript `int` is a signed 64-bit value, so mask shifts and compare as unsigned.

### 3. Weighted drop table

```python
def weighted_pick(rng, table):           # table: list of (item, weight); weights are relative
    total = sum(w for _, w in table)
    roll = rng.uniform(0, total)
    upto = 0.0
    for item, w in table:
        upto += w
        if roll < upto:
            return item
    return next(i for i, w in reversed(table) if w > 0)  # roll == total (float edge)
```

Built-ins do the same: Python `rng.choices(items, weights)`, Godot
`rng.rand_weighted(PackedFloat32Array(weights))` (returns an index). Pure rolls produce streaks;
for a guaranteed rate use a bag or pity timer (`references/dungeon-generation.md`).

### 4. Seed sweep (determinism, connectivity, distribution)

```python
import hashlib, json, random, statistics

def sweep(generate, seeds=range(200), spawn=None):
    """generate(rng) -> grid (0 wall, 1 floor, solid border). Prints and returns a report."""
    bad, ratios, digests = [], [], set()
    for seed in seeds:
        grid = generate(random.Random(seed))
        if grid != generate(random.Random(seed)):
            bad.append((seed, "not deterministic"))
            continue
        floor = [(x, y) for y, row in enumerate(grid) for x, v in enumerate(row) if v]
        if not floor:
            bad.append((seed, "no floor"))
            continue
        start = spawn(grid) if spawn else floor[0]
        if len(reachable_floor(grid, start)) != len(floor):   # from dungeon-generation.md
            bad.append((seed, "unreachable floor"))
        ratios.append(len(floor) / (len(grid) * len(grid[0])))
        digests.add(hashlib.sha1(json.dumps(grid).encode()).hexdigest())
    report = {"seeds": len(seeds), "failure_count": len(bad), "failures": bad[:10],
              "distinct_maps": len(digests),
              "floor_ratio": (min(ratios), statistics.median(ratios), max(ratios)) if ratios else None}
    print(report)
    return report

# report = sweep(lambda rng: drunkard(40, 30, rng)); raise SystemExit(report["failure_count"] > 0)
```

Run it twice in separate processes and compare the digests too: that catches hash-randomized
set order and other per-process state that a same-process rerun cannot see. Add the checks your
game needs (spawn not in a hazard, exit reachable, key before its door) as more `bad.append`
lines.

## Check it

1. Run the seed sweep over at least 200 seeds: zero failures, and `distinct_maps` close to the
   seed count (a low number means the seed is not reaching the generator).
2. Run it again in a new process (`PYTHONHASHSEED` differs per run by default) and confirm the
   same digests for the same seeds.
3. If seeds are shared or saved, pin the first outputs of the PRNG in a test (Pattern 2).
4. For engine-side generators, port the sweep to a headless test (Godot: follow
   `godot-gdscript-headless-testing`) and print the same report.
5. Ask the user to play a handful of named seeds and report any map that felt broken, samey or
   unfair, with its seed, so you can replay it.

## Gotchas

- **Global RNG inside generation** makes worlds unreproducible the moment call order changes.
- **Iterating a set or dict of strings** (Python `rng.choice(list(some_set))`) changes order per
  process because of hash randomization. Sort first.
- **Seeds that stop matching after an update.** Python guarantees only `random()` across
  versions (not `randint` or `choice`), .NET says `System.Random` may change between major
  versions, and Godot calls its PCG32 an implementation detail. Ship your own PRNG (Pattern 2)
  or save the generated result instead of the seed.
- **One stream for everything**: adding one decoration roll reshuffles every later room. Derive
  per-system child seeds.
- **Correlated noise fields**: elevation and moisture from the same seed and offset make biomes
  line up in bands. Reseed or offset each field.
- **Octave sums out of range**: divide by the summed amplitude, and know the library's range
  (FastNoiseLite and `noise.snoise` are about -1..1, `Mathf.PerlinNoise` about 0..1).
- **Flat noise at integer coordinates**: Perlin noise is 0 at every lattice point, so raw
  `noise(x, y)` at whole tile coordinates is constant. Scale by a non-integer frequency;
  FastNoiseLite applies its `frequency` (default 0.01) for you.
- **No connectivity check**: isolated rooms and caves. Flood-fill from the spawn and reject or
  reconnect, and re-check after smoothing passes, which can split regions.
- **Unbounded placement loops** ("keep trying until N rooms fit") can spin forever on a small
  grid. Cap attempts and accept fewer rooms.
- **WFC contradictions on every run** usually mean asymmetric adjacency rules: if B may sit east
  of A, A must be allowed west of B.

## References

- `references/dungeon-generation.md`: read when implementing rooms and corridors, BSP,
  drunkard's walk or cellular caves, wave function collapse, the `reachable_floor` flood fill,
  or bag and pity distributions. Its Python is tested by the repo.
- `references/noise.md`: read when building terrain or biomes: frequency, octaves,
  redistribution, ridges and terraces, two-field biome lookup, island shaping, scatter
  placement, and seamless wraparound.

## Related skills

- `roguelike`, `survival-crafting`: genres that decide what to generate and when.
- `level-design`: authored pacing that generation complements, and the key-order check.
- `godot-tilemap`, `unity-tilemap-2d`: painting the grid; `game-ai`: pathfinding over it.
- `save-systems`: storing the seed and generator version, or the generated result.

## Version notes

Last verified: 2026-11-11.

- Python `random`: only `random()` is guaranteed to repeat across versions for a given seed
  (https://docs.python.org/3/library/random.html#notes-on-reproducibility).
- .NET `System.Random`: the algorithm may change between major versions
  (https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/dotnet/api/system.random).
- Godot 4.7 `RandomNumberGenerator`: PCG32 today, documented as an implementation detail;
  `rand_weighted` exists; `FastNoiseLite.frequency` defaults to 0.01
  (https://github.com/godotengine/godot/blob/4.7-stable/doc/classes/RandomNumberGenerator.xml).
- The seed sweep and SplitMix64 outputs were run on Python 3.12.

skills.name: gh-gd-roblox-characters
skills.description: Roblox player characters: CharacterAdded lifecycle, Humanoid and HumanoidRootPart, R6, R15 and custom rigs, respawn and Tools. Use when a character script breaks after respawn, animations do not play or replicate, or sprint code fights the Humanoid. Not for hit validation (`roblox-networking`), forces and raycasts (`roblox-physics`) or cameras (`camera-systems`).
skills.body:
# Roblox characters

A `Player` is the durable identity; each `Character` is a replaceable session with its own
references, connections, animation tracks, and cleanup. Most character bugs are one character's
state leaking into the next.

## Workflow

1. **Read the character contract.** Avatar Settings (rig type, movement system), `StarterCharacter`,
   `StarterCharacterScripts`, `Players.CharacterAutoLoads`, `Workspace.PlayerCharacterDestroyBehavior`,
   the existing Animate or controller scripts, tools, tags, and collision groups. Extend what is
   there; do not add a second controller.
2. **Separate scopes.** Player-scope state survives respawn; character-scope state does not. Put
   each character's connections, tracks, and temporary instances in one cleanup scope.
3. **Bind existing and future characters.** Connect `CharacterAdded`, then bind `player.Character`
   if it already exists. On the server, do this for players already in `Players:GetPlayers()`.
4. **Resolve parts defensively.** `WaitForChild` with a timeout for `Humanoid`, the root part, and
   `Animator`; after every yield, check the character is still the current one before acting.
5. **Choose one movement owner per state.** Standard avatars use Humanoid movement or the
   Character Controller Library. Physical mechanics (dash, knockback, grapple) use an impulse or a
   constraint for their duration and hand control back cleanly.
6. **Own animation lifecycle.** Load through the rig's `Animator`, keep tracks and marker
   connections in the character scope, and stop them on cleanup. Markers drive presentation; any
   gameplay effect they trigger is validated on the server.
7. **Run the lifecycle check.** With the Studio MCP server connected, start play, respawn the
   player several times from `execute_luau` on the `Server` datamodel
   (`for _ = 1, 5 do player:LoadCharacterAsync() task.wait(1) end`), then read
   `get_console_output`: expect no errors and exactly one setup log per spawn. Without MCP, ask the
   user to reset five times in Test and once with two players in Server & Clients, and to report
   duplicated logs, stuck animations, or errors.

## Pattern: replaceable character scope

```lua
local Players = game:GetService("Players")
local player = Players.LocalPlayer
local generation = 0
local connections: {RBXScriptConnection} = {}
local currentCharacter: Model? = nil

local function clearCharacter()
    generation += 1
    for _, connection in connections do connection:Disconnect() end
    table.clear(connections)
    currentCharacter = nil
end

local function bindCharacter(character: Model)
    -- Guard before teardown: a stale call must not clear a binding that is already current.
    if player.Character ~= character or currentCharacter == character then return end
    clearCharacter()
    currentCharacter = character
    local thisGeneration = generation
    local humanoid = character:WaitForChild("Humanoid", 10)
    local root = character:WaitForChild("HumanoidRootPart", 10)
    -- A respawn during WaitForChild bumps generation and makes this call stale.
    if not humanoid or not root or generation ~= thisGeneration then return end

    table.insert(connections, humanoid.Died:Connect(function()
        if generation ~= thisGeneration then return end
        setCharacterUiEnabled(false)
    end))
    attachCurrentCharacterSystems(character, humanoid, root)
end

player.CharacterRemoving:Connect(function(character)
    if currentCharacter == character then clearCharacter() end
end)
player.CharacterAdded:Connect(bindCharacter)
if player.Character then task.defer(bindCharacter, player.Character) end
```

Use the project's cleanup utility when one exists rather than introducing a framework for three
connections. Server systems repeat this binding per `Player` and clear player-scope tables on
`PlayerRemoving`.

## Pattern: animation through Animator and markers

```lua
local animation = Instance.new("Animation")
animation.AnimationId = "rbxassetid://1234567890"
local track = animator:LoadAnimation(animation)
local markerConnection = track:GetMarkerReachedSignal("Commit"):Connect(function(parameter)
    playLocalSwingEffect(parameter) -- presentation only; the server validates any hit
end)

track:Play(0.1)
-- On character teardown:
markerConnection:Disconnect()
track:Stop(0.1)
animation:Destroy()
```

Rigs without a `Humanoid` need an `AnimationController` with an `Animator`. `Humanoid:LoadAnimation()`
is deprecated; always load through the `Animator`.

## Movement and rig rules

- If R6 is supported, do not hardcode R15 limb names. Prefer attachments, tags, or a small rig
  adapter; branch on `Humanoid.RigType` only where topology really differs.
- `HumanoidRootPart` is the usual assembly root, not a guarantee for custom models. Write down the
  custom rig contract and validate it at spawn.
- Setting `AssemblyLinearVelocity` is an instant change; use `ApplyImpulse` for one-off pushes and
  a `LinearVelocity` constraint for sustained control (details in `roblox-physics`).
- For new actions such as sprint or rebinding jump, use the Input Action System (`InputContext`,
  `InputAction`, `InputBinding`) instead of raw `UserInputService` hooks. Give your context a higher
  `Priority` (and `Sink`) than the default player contexts so it wins.
- If the place uses the Character Controller Library (Avatar Settings → Movement → Abilities) or a
  `ControllerManager`, extend its abilities and controllers. Layering `HumanoidStateType` changes
  on top of it fights the library.
- Tools move between `Backpack` and the character on equip. Listen to ancestry and the tool's
  `Equipped`/`Unequipped` events instead of assuming one parent.
- Change appearance with `Humanoid:ApplyDescriptionAsync()` and keep the applied
  `HumanoidDescription` up to date.
- Under Server Authority (`Workspace.AuthorityMode = Server`), gameplay animation runs inside
  bound simulation functions and the client may replace tracks during rollback, so look tracks up
  each frame with `Animator:GetTrackByAnimationId()` instead of caching them. Tools are not fully
  supported there yet; see `roblox-networking`.

## Gotchas

| Symptom | Likely cause | Remedy |
|---|---|---|
| works once, breaks after reset | cached character, Humanoid or root | rebuild per `CharacterAdded`; clear on removal |
| callbacks fire twice after deaths | old character connections survived | character-scoped cleanup plus generation checks |
| memory grows with every respawn | old characters are only unparented, and tables still reference them | clear Instance-keyed tables; check `PlayerCharacterDestroyBehavior` |
| delayed setup edits the wrong rig | async work outlived its spawn | compare current character or generation after every yield |
| animation plays only locally or not at all | wrong Animator, side, or asset permission | inspect the rig's Animator, who loads it, and the asset owner |
| hit marker awards impossible hits | marker trusted as authority | marker for timing; server validates combat state |
| R6 or custom rig errors | R15 names assumed | rig contract and adapter; test every supported rig |
| tool disappears from a system | fixed Backpack or Character parent assumed | handle equip, unequip, and character replacement |
| custom force fights the Humanoid | two controllers own motion | one movement owner per state; restore on exit |

## Resources

- Read `references/lifecycle-and-animation.md` when a system spans respawns, supports several
  rigs, or owns animation and tool resources: server binding, death vs removal, custom-character
  checklist, and the lifecycle stress matrix.

## Related skills

- `roblox-physics`: forces, constraints, assemblies, and network ownership.
- `roblox-networking`: validating character actions and rejecting stale requests.
- `input-systems`: action mapping and responsive movement intent.
- `camera-systems`: cameras that follow a replaceable character.

## Version notes

Last verified: 2026-11-11.

- `Player:LoadCharacter()`, `Humanoid:ApplyDescription()` and `Humanoid:PlayEmote()` are deprecated
  in favour of `LoadCharacterAsync()`, `ApplyDescriptionAsync()` and `PlayEmoteAsync()`.
- The Character Controller Library was announced as released for live experiences in April 2026;
  its docs page still carried a beta note on the verification date. Avatar Settings needs a saved
  or published place.
- `Workspace.PlayerCharacterDestroyBehavior`, when enabled, destroys the old character on respawn
  and the `Player` object on leave.
- To re-check an API: append `.md` to its Creator Hub URL, or start from
  `https://create.roblox.com/docs/llms.txt`.

Sources: `https://create.roblox.com/docs/characters`,
`https://create.roblox.com/docs/animation/using`,
`https://create.roblox.com/docs/characters/character-controller-library`,
`https://create.roblox.com/docs/reference/engine/classes/Player`,
`https://create.roblox.com/docs/reference/engine/classes/Humanoid`,
`https://create.roblox.com/docs/reference/engine/classes/Workspace`,
`https://create.roblox.com/docs/projects/server-authority`,
`https://devforum.roblox.com/t/full-release-the-future-of-character-movement-character-controller-library/4565267`.
